originalTitle: Field and French flourish for Wigan to boost title charge with victory at Leigh
summary: Tries from Jai Field and Bevan French sparked Wigan’s 20-8 victory at Leigh to move them up to second in Super League and boost their title credentials
content: There are moments in Super League seasons, marathons as they are, which can often prove to be sliding doors occasions for both teams involved. And as the full-time hooter sounded in Leigh and Wigan celebrated another statement win with their travelling support, it was not difficult to imagine how one particular moment from this derby could swing the seasons of both teams. For nearly 40 minutes, Leigh had done something no team had managed to do to Wigan for quite some time: make them appear second best. The Warriors, on a run of nine consecutive wins which began with their Challenge Cup triumph at Wembley in May, had been completely outplayed by their local rivals and their own coach admitted they were lucky to be only 8-0 behind. But great teams, and great players, find a way to win. Leigh’s first real mistake came two minutes before half-time, when they turned their backs on Jai Field after conceding a penalty, expecting Wigan to kick for touch. Instead, Field tapped the ball and raced 90m downfield to reduce the deficit to just two points by half-time. Just like that, it turned. When Leigh produced another error three minutes after the restart, the Warriors’ other talisman, Bevan French, pounced to inexplicably move Wigan ahead in a game they had been dominated in to that point. Two more Leigh knock-ons followed soon afterwards and once again, the visitors scored tries from both of them. Nobody knows how this would have ended had Leigh led more convincingly at half-time. If the Leopards had won, they would have inserted themselves into the picture for the top two. Instead, they are now sitting sixth and looking nervously over their shoulders. Wigan, meanwhile, march on – they are now second and just two points behind the league leaders, Leeds. Perhaps in a way it was a lesson as to the step Leigh still need to take to compete with a side like Wigan. But the Warriors, frustrated as they will be by the level of this performance, should take great heart from the fact that if they can be this below par with the ball and still win against a playoff rival, imagine what they can do if it clicks in a playoff tie this autumn. “We needed to improve because in that first half we were second best,” their coach, Matt Peet, said. “We’ve managed our way out of a situation there. There was nothing wrong with our effort but they were very good. You don’t want to win this way every week but it’s good to know it’s in the locker.” Leigh deservedly led by eight points early on thanks to Innes Senior’s outstanding try and two goals from the boot of Adam Cook, but there was no doubting the big moment here – Field’s breakaway try – left a mark on them. The Leopards will hope it does not leave any long-lasting damage in their push to make the playoffs again. “I went in and tried to lift them at half-time but it felt like that moment was a bit of an implosion,” Leigh’s coach, Adrian Lam, said. “It was hard to watch in the second half but we were awesome in that first half. It was unbelievably good, and we are very close to being very good. A bit of negativity crept in and our gameplan just fell apart.” Field’s and French’s tries turned an eight-point deficit into a lead either side of half-time. When Leigh turned possession over cheaply again, Zach Eckersley was the third grateful recipient of a momentary lapse from the Leopards. Then as the hour mark struck, Noah Hodkinson was afforded the same opportunity to make it 20-8 and from there, Wigan were wise enough defensively to close out a crucial win. But this was a captivating and engrossing derby. With the National Rugby League’s bid for control of Super League incoming over the next few days, this was an advert for everything that is great about the competition. A sold-out stadium, a local rivalry and star talent proving to be the difference when it mattered most. Yet for all the change potentially coming Super League’s way off the field, one constant is that it would take a brave man to back against Wigan prevailing at Old Trafford again in October.
chineseTitle: 菲尔德和法国队在利的胜利为维冈队带来了冠军头衔
chineseSummary: 杰伊·菲尔德和贝文·弗伦奇的射门帮助维冈队以 20-8 战胜利，使他们在超级联赛中排名第二，并提高了他们的冠军资格
chineseContent: 在超级联赛赛季中，有些时刻就像马拉松比赛一样，通常可以证明是两支球队的滑动门时刻。随着全场哨声响起，维冈队在客场支持下庆祝另一场胜利，不难想象这场德比中的一个特殊时刻将如何改变两支球队的赛季。在近 40 分钟的时间里，利做了一件很长一段时间以来没有任何一支球队能够对维冈做到的事情：让他们看起来第二好。勇士队从五月份在温布利赢得挑战杯开始，已经取得了九连胜，但他们完全被当地的对手击败，他们自己的教练承认他们很幸运，只落后 8-0。但伟大的球队和伟大的球员总会找到获胜的方法。利的第一个真正的错误发生在半场结束前两分钟，当时他们在丢了一个点球后背对着杰·菲尔德，期待维冈队踢球。相反，菲尔德接球并向前场冲刺 90m，半场结束时将比分差距缩小到仅两分。就这样，它转了。当利在比赛重新开始三分钟后再次出现失误时，勇士队的另一位护身符贝文·弗伦奇突然出手，莫名其妙地帮助维冈队在一场比赛中取得了领先，而这场比赛他们此前一直处于主导地位。不久之后，李又两次射门，客队再次从两人的射门中得分。没有人知道如果利在中场休息时更有说服力地领先的话，比赛会如何结束。如果美洲豹队获胜，他们将跻身前两名。相反，他们现在坐在第六位，紧张地回头望去。与此同时，维冈继续前进——他们现在排名第二，仅落后联赛领头羊利兹联两分。也许在某种程度上它是
